facts: Oldest surviving chapter
The first recorded road.
This date is preserved as an archive working date, not an unquestionable historical timestamp.

Alterra stands at the beginning of the early recorded plugin era: the first known playthrough where the archive can still trace players, settlement growth, technical ambition and disaster into one coherent origin record.

Sunstar 47, Tony and Wade did not begin with a metropolis. They began with a comparatively small settlement and slowly transformed it into Alterra — a fast-developing technological city shaped by infrastructure, administration, trade, security, military experimentation and increasingly serious defensive construction.

The surviving record matters because it establishes a pattern that would echo through later Aevum history: ordinary places becoming major locations through player action, systems, conflict and memory.
City growth
The village that became a city.
Alterra expanded in layers rather than appearing fully formed.
Village
A small original settlement formed the earliest known core. Near it, the players established a controlled military tract.
Fortified core
Metal fencing, a smaller stone defensive wall and controlled military space protected the early operational area.
Inner expansion
The old village became increasingly important as development grew around it and new fortified sections formed behind fresh walls.
Outer Alterra
Eventually the city pushed beyond the older defenses, creating large developed areas outside the original fortifications.
Founders / Players
Three foundations.
Each player shaped a different side of Alterra's rise.
Administration
Sunstar 47

Sunstar 47 was effectively the organizational backbone of Alterra. His work covered administration, trade agreements, outside relations, city organization and the systems that kept the growing settlement functioning.
He represented the civic side of Alterra's rise: the part that turned expansion into something that could be coordinated, sustained and recognized.
Technology / Military
Tony

Tony focused heavily on technological development, military advancement, defensive systems and new infrastructure. One of the most important records from this era is the first early appearance of J.A.R.V.I.S.
This page does not fold later Vault 8 history into Alterra, but the connection is visible in hindsight.
Covert protection
Wade
Wade followed a more independent path. As a hitman, he was not primarily the public administrator or the visible builder of great systems.
His role was quieter: dealing with threats, protecting Alterra from the background and operating away from the city's visible political structure.
City at its height
A city in acceleration.
Alterra stopped feeling like three players upgrading a village. It became a city-state-like urban project with districts, defenses, trade, organization and technological infrastructure.
The archive does not preserve exact population figures. What it does preserve is the direction of growth: village → fortified settlement → city → large technological metropolis.
Military Alterra
The concealed protection bunker.
The military tract existed from very early in Alterra's history and remained important as the city expanded. Tony's work pushed the military and defensive side of the city forward.

Alterra eventually possessed a highly advanced concealed protection bunker — a protected fallback structure important for its era and a thematic ancestor to the much larger bunker and Vault projects that later shaped Tony's history.
Early artificial intelligence
The First J.A.R.V.I.S.

During the Alterra era, Tony developed J.A.R.V.I.S., an artificial intelligence that would remain connected to Tony's story far beyond this first playthrough. In hindsight, this is one of the most important technical origins preserved in the first record.
First nuclear catastrophe
The record turns dark.
Growth and technical optimism gave way to war, radiation, loss and survival.
The first great disaster
A major war occurred during the playthrough. The archive does not identify every side or cause, but it preserves the result: early server history experienced its first major nuclear catastrophe.
This event marks a clear break in the Alterra record. The world was no longer only expanding; it had become capable of large-scale ruin.
NPC memorial
John — Weapons Developer
John was one of the most important NPCs of the Alterra era, an exceptionally talented weapons developer regarded as one of the finest of his time.

When the nuclear catastrophe struck, John failed to reach the Vault or shelter in time. He died from radioactive exposure, becoming one of the earliest major named NPC deaths preserved by the archive.
Final chapter
The Vault Incident.
The end did not arrive as a clean single explosion.
The final collapse began when the players entered or interacted with a Vault-like location containing dangerous, carcinogenic fruits. They attempted to retrieve them — but took far too many.
Whatever watched over the Vault did not tolerate what had been taken. The surviving archive does not identify the force within the Vault, and this page does not pretend otherwise.
Afterward, strange creatures began appearing in the Overworld. They spread into the world, poisoned their surroundings and contaminated the environment until the situation spiraled beyond recovery.

Legacy
Why Alterra still matters.

Alterra is one of the earliest major player-built cities preserved by the archive. It introduced long-running themes: Tony's recurring technological history, the origin of J.A.R.V.I.S., protected bunker concepts, large-scale catastrophe and the transformation of ordinary settlements into locations with identity.

Canon update: Alterra carries Eternal Status. Its record did not end as a forgotten ruin; it remains one of the largest companies on the Desagment Plugin and one of the earliest examples of a player-made place surviving as a major institutional power.
Recovered timeline
The first record, in order.
A compact reconstruction from surviving notes.
Small Village The original settlement is discovered and developed.
Military Tract Established Metal fencing, stone defenses and controlled space protect early military development.
Alterra Expands The village becomes the city center as new districts and outer areas appear.
J.A.R.V.I.S. Developed Tony creates the early AI system tied to later records.
Concealed Bunker Era Advanced defensive infrastructure emerges.
Nuclear Catastrophe A major war causes the first great nuclear disaster of the era.
Death of John The weapons developer fails to reach shelter and dies from radiation.
Vault Incident Too many dangerous fruits are removed from a Vault-like location.
Overworld Contamination Creatures emerge, corrupt surroundings and make recovery impossible.
End of Playthrough I The first record closes.
Mountain origin
Before Vault 8.
Tony's road began with travel, an isolated village and an unexpected understanding.
The same Tony returns
This was the same Tony and the same continuing soul in another body. His descent from Magnus Bane made repeated reincarnation possible.
Deadshot's village
The settlement between the mountains was controlled by the feared sniper Deadshot, who eventually entrusted it to Tony.
J.A.R.V.I.S. installed
Tony placed J.A.R.V.I.S. inside a mainframe. The AI terraformed the mountain into a sealed complex.
Underground city
Inside the mountain.
Vault 8 was never a narrow concrete shelter.
A city below ground
Full houses and buildings roughly eight or nine stories high stood within the mountain complex.
Military Wing
An enormous military sector connected to at least about forty nuclear silos and further defensive facilities.
D-Day
Tony's beach military base was linked to the wider system and produced ships among its other functions.
Fortification
Parts of the structure used materials comparable to Stonebricks Mark 40.
The shell was designed to resist extreme explosions, including an external nuclear strike.
Massively reinforced doors, security systems and military defenses made a conventional capture nearly impossible.
Wade helped in the early phase, then disappeared; Tony and J.A.R.V.I.S. continued the greater project alone.
Broken continuity
The destroyed timelines.
This playthrough did not receive one clean ending.
The Apex Predator assault
Tony killed the son of Cuban Bliss. The Apex Predators answered by attacking Vault 8, bombarding it with Titans and eventually detonating a nuclear weapon inside the complex. The Vault was destroyed.
Magnus Bane's hidden corrections
Tony should have died with the destroyed Vault.
Magnus Bane intervened, saved him and turned the timeline back.
Tony did not yet know that Magnus Bane was his father.
Later catastrophes drew further hidden interventions and corrected timelines.
Damaged and unplayable world states eventually ended the run in practice without producing one final canonical ending.
Persistent location
Vault 8 remains.
The Vault continues to exist in canon and can persist across servers, developing beyond an active playthrough. Finding it remains extraordinarily unlikely.
Fading inheritance
Tony's next return.
Repeated reincarnations and long separation from Magnus Bane have weakened Tony's former advantage. Another return after his latest death is possible, but no longer guaranteed.
Founding
The rise of Temmie Town.
A peaceful change of leadership became the beginning of a city.
Growth under pressure
The first work centered on houses and civic infrastructure.
Armed raiders attacked regularly, forcing OBAMA, Tony and Faaram to defend the settlement with firearms.
The city's economic importance grew alongside its size.
A major Obamacare headquarters and another large Obamacare building employed many people.
Temmie Town repeatedly attracted events far stranger than an ordinary city should survive.
Anomaly record
The city that drew the impossible.
Rifts, creatures and curses found Temmie Town again and again.
The world rift
A tear appeared without a known cause. Vast numbers of demonic spiders poured through it and attacked the surrounding land. Skeletal horses and further anomalies appeared at other times.
The Three-Headed Sunflower

A gigantic mutated sunflower grew on Obamacare property. It was friendly toward OBAMA, yet powerful enough to devastate approximately 97% of Russia before Satoru Gojo intervened and removed the curse.
Each head contained one Sukuna finger. Three fingers were recovered and taken after the curse was removed. The Archive does not invent further combat details.
Hidden protector
Uwubama and the rewritten city.
The repeated return of Temmie Town was not a simple reset.
Reality in service of survival
Uwubama began as a clone of OBAMA and developed control over time, timelines, realities and the multiverse.
His central goal was that OBAMA and his friends should be safe.
When a timeline ended in catastrophe, a later playthrough could open with Temmie Town and its people restored.
The city sometimes continued to develop between these apparent endings.
Uwubama had altered reality behind the scenes.
Persistent location
Eternal City.
Temmie Town can persist and continue developing across server instances and playthrough contexts. It is not literally indestructible: full destruction could end that persistence.
No active player character currently lives there.
Uwubama's end
Almost erased.

The Time Gods intervened after too many violations of time, reality and multiverse. Uwubama was erased — almost completely. A fragment of his brain remains, leaving restoration theoretically possible rather than promised.
Known ending
The previous road was brought to an end by the Aizen event. Its full truth remains sealed, but the opened shape is clear enough: a released force became the end of that path.
Remaining echoes
Older names such as OBAMA, Faaram, Raven, Tony and Jawohl remain in the archive because their stories still carry weight, even when their path is no longer active.
Opened sequence
Faaram once stood before the Overlord and received the rare mark now catalogued as Overlord's Grace.
That mark drew old attention toward the world and left the road more fragile than it seemed.
Aizen was released to strike Meruem, the Chimera Ant King.
The released blade did not remain a simple answer. The Aizen event ended this former Pre-Fusion Continuity, not the current multiverse.
